source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: Two suffixes will be considered: 1) /-TYj/ which has variants /-sYj/, /-lYj/, /-nYj/ and 2) /–msYj/. It will be argued that /-TYj/- and /-msYj/-suffixation has syntactic status. For the first suffix this assumption receives support from the presence of some degree of meaning fluctuation with verbal derivatives as well as from the fact that the suffix can attach not only bare nouns but also to regular (i.e. non-idiomatic) AP-NP combinations (52)-(53).
